messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High 5xx rate and request queueing detected on dedicated pool `dedicated-eu-1`. Threshold: 5xx rate > 3% for 3m. Paging maya (oncall).

maya: ack, I'm on it. seeing a big inbound spike on the throughput graph and the pool's queued requests. opening the runbook.

ashok: I can look at autoscale knobs. current pool config: min=4, desired=6, max=12, burst=false. Looks like token bucket exhausted for some backends.

maya: root cause hypothesis — sudden traffic surge from a single partner (org 82314) plus long tail requests causing KV cache churn and larger per-request GPU time.

ryan: Noted. If we flip burst capacity it should allow immediate extra capacity while autoscaler ramps. We can also apply per-org throttles as temporary mitigation.

autoscale-bot: Autoscaler event: scale-up requested -> target replicas=10, expected by 1772040300 (7m). Current pending pods: 2.

maya: let's enable burst for 30m and add a soft rate limit for noisy orgs. ashok — can you toggle burst? include command you run so SRE audit sees it.

ashok: running toggle now. command: ```
POST /internal/api/dedicated/pools/dedicated-eu-1/burst
Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN
Body: {"enable": true, "duration_minutes": 30, "reason": "traffic surge - autoscale delay"}
```

ashok: cli output: ```
{"status":"ok","pool":"dedicated-eu-1","burst_enabled":true,"expires_at":"2026-03-15T15:15:23Z"}
```

maya: confirmed in console: burst enabled. dispatching traffic to new instances.

olivia: adding per-org throttle for org 82314 to 5 rps (was 25 rps). Doing a soft reject (429) with Retry-After so partner can backoff.

ryan: config snippet for quota override we used: ```json
{"org_id":"82314","quota":{"requests_per_second":5},"scope":"pool:dedi-eu-1","expires_at":"2026-03-15T15:20:00Z"}
```

maya: applying a temporary global per-route token-bucket for long-running /completions calls: 100 concurrent -> 80 concurrent, to protect KV cache.

incident-bot: Customer impact summary: ~12 customers saw intermittent 503/502; major customers: partner-ACME (org 82314), beta-team-1 (org 9102). Automated notifications sent to affected accounts.

ashok: monitoring metrics: p50 latency back to normal, p95 still elevated. queued requests dropped from 420 -> 60 after burst enabled and throttle applied.

maya: good. any risky side-effects from burst? Ryan?

ryan: burst increases allowed capacity but bypasses some allocation guarantees — cost impact and potential downstream hot-sharding. safe for 30m while autoscaler completes. keep an eye on GPU memory fragmentation.

olivia: also flagged: if KV cache miss rate doesn't drop, we may need to disable a heavy reranking feature for affected models (temporary feature flag off).

maya: do it if miss rate stays > 10% for 10m. ashok, can you stand by to roll the flag? include rollback command.

ashok: feature flag commands: ```
# disable reranker
PATCH /internal/api/flags/re-ranking
Body: {"enabled": false, "scope":"pool:dedi-eu-1","reason":"incident mitigation"}
# rollback
PATCH /internal/api/flags/re-ranking
Body: {"enabled": true}
```

olivia: I'm preparing a customer-facing blurb for status page. Short summary: "We observed elevated errors in Europe due to a traffic surge affecting Dedicated pool dedicated-eu-1. We enabled burst capacity and applied temporary throttles. Monitoring ongoing."

maya: great. doing a quick handoff to olivia in 10m. I'll summarize: enabled burst for 30m, quota override for org 82314, decreased concurrency for /completions, autoscaler still scaling towards 10. If p95 doesn't drop to < 1.2s in 15m, disable reranker.

olivia: ack — taking over. will monitor for 1h and update status every 15m. setting a reminder: `/remind @olivia check dedicated-eu-1 metrics in 15m`

autoscale-bot: Scale-up complete: replicas=10 at 1772040450.

olivia: seeing p95 drop to 0.95s, queue at ~20. keeping burst enabled for now but will let it expire at 15:15 unless we extend.

maya: thanks team. follow-up action items: 1) investigate partner 82314 spikes (SE outreach), 2) consider autoscaler tuning for faster ramp on dedicated pools, 3) postmortem if this repeats.

olivia: I'll update the incident channel and set up a short post-incident meeting if we see recurrence. marking this thread as monitoring. :white_check_mark:
